questions.q: What is the remainder when $7^n-6 n$ is divided by 36 for $n=100$ ?
questions.solution:
Suppose $\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{n})=7^{\mathrm{n}}-6 \mathrm{n}=(6+1)^{\mathrm{n}}-6 \mathrm{n}$
Using Binomial expansion, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& =1+6 n+{ }^n c_2 6^2+{ }^n c_3 6^3+\ldots . .+6^n-6 n \\
& =1+6^2\left({ }^n c_2+{ }^n c_2 \times 6+\ldots .+6^{n-2}\right) \\
& =1+36\left({ }^{100} c_2+{ }^{100} c_2 \times 6+\ldots .+6^{98}\right)\{\because n=100\} \\
& =1+36 \mathrm{~m} \text { where } \mathrm{m}={ }^{100} c_2+{ }^{100} c_2 \times 6+\ldots . .+6^{98}
\end{aligned}$
So, when $7^{\mathrm{n}}-6 \mathrm{n}$ is divided by 36 , the remainder will be 1.

Paragraph: Let $(8+3 \sqrt{7})^{20}=\mathrm{U}+\mathrm{V}$ and $(8-3 \sqrt{7})^{20}=\mathrm{W}$, where U is an integer and $0 \lt \mathrm{V} \lt 1$.
Question: What is $\mathrm{V}+\mathrm{W}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
We have, $(8+3 \sqrt{7})^{20}=\mathrm{U}+\mathrm{V}$....(i)
and $(8-3 \sqrt{7})^{20}=\mathrm{W}$....(ii)
Here, $\mathrm{o} \lt  \mathrm{W} \lt  1$
Now, adding equation (i) \& (ii), we have,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{U}+\mathrm{V}+\mathrm{W}=(8+3 \sqrt{7})^{20}+(8-3 \sqrt{7})^{20} \\
& =2\left[{ }^{20} \mathrm{C}_0 \cdot 8^{20}+{ }^{20} \mathrm{C}_2 8^{18} \cdot(3 \sqrt{7})^2+\ldots .+(3 \sqrt{7})^{20}\right]
\end{aligned}$
R.H.S. is an even number.
Also, $\mathrm{o} \lt  \mathrm{V} \lt  1, \mathrm{o} \lt  \mathrm{W} \lt  1$ and U is an integer
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}+\mathrm{W}$ is an integer $\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}+\mathrm{W}=1$
So, $V+W=1$

& =\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{2\left(1+\tan \frac{x}{2}\right)} d x \\
& \text { let } 1+\tan \frac{x}{2}=t \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \sec ^2 \frac{x}{2} d x=d t
\end{aligned}$
when $\mathrm{x}=\pi / 2$ then $\mathrm{t}=2$, and when $\mathrm{x}=0$ then $\mathrm{t}=1=\int_1^2 \frac{1}{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt}=[\ln \mathrm{t}]_1^2=\ln 2-\ln 1=\ln 2$

& \text { Now, } \sum_{n=1}^4 D_n=200 \sum_{n=1}^4\left(-n+2 n^2-n^3\right) \\
& \because \sum n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}, \sum n^2=\frac{n(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6} \\
& \sum n^3=\left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right]^2
\end{aligned}$
Hence,
$\begin{aligned}
& \sum_{n=1}^4 D_n=200\left[-\frac{(4)(5)}{2}+2 \cdot \frac{(4)(5)(9)}{6}-\left(\frac{(4)(5)}{2}\right)^2\right] \\
& =200(-50)=-10000
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $A$ and $B$ be two square matrices of same order. If $A B$ is a null matrix, then which one of the following is correct?
options: Both A and B are null matrices
Either A or B is a null matrix
B is a null matrix if A is a non-singular matrix
questions.solution:
We have, $\mathrm{AB}=0$
Let $A=\left[\begin{array}{ll}a & b \\ c & d\end{array}\right]$ and $B=\left[\begin{array}{ll}p & q \\ r & s\end{array}\right]$
So, $\mathrm{AB}=\left[\begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{a} & \mathrm{b} \\ \mathrm{c} & \mathrm{d}\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{p} & \mathrm{q} \\ \mathrm{r} & \mathrm{s}\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ll}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\Rightarrow\left[\begin{array}{ll}
\mathrm{ap}+\mathrm{br} & \mathrm{aq}+\mathrm{bs} \\
\mathrm{cp}+\mathrm{dr} & \mathrm{cq}+\mathrm{ds}
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ll}
0 & 0 \\
0 & 0
\end{array}\right]$
Comparing both sides, we have
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{ap}+\mathrm{br}=0 ....(i)\\
& \mathrm{aq}+\mathrm{bs}=0 ....(ii)\\
& \mathrm{cp}+\mathrm{dr}=0 ....(iii)\\
& \mathrm{cq}+\mathrm{ds}=0 ....(iv)
\end{aligned}$
Solving equation (i) and (iii), we get
$(\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}) \mathrm{p}=0$ and $(\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}) \mathrm{r}=0$
Solving equation (ii) amd (iv), we get
$(\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}) \mathrm{q}=0 \text { and }(\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}) \mathrm{s}=0$
Now, If A is non-singular $\Rightarrow \mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc} \neq 0$.
So, we get, $p=q=r=s=0$
So, B is a null matrix.

B. $\cot 22.5^{\circ}$

Let $\mathrm{t}=\tan 22.5^{\circ}=\tan \frac{45^{\circ}}{2}$
Now, $\tan 45^{\circ}=\tan \left(2 \times \frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}=\frac{2 \tan \left(\frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}}{1-\tan ^2\left(\frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 1=\frac{2 t}{1-t^2} \Rightarrow t^2+2 t-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow t=\frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4+4}}{2}=-1 \pm \sqrt{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \tan \left(\frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}=-1 \pm \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow \tan \left(\frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}=-1+(\sqrt{2})
\end{aligned}\left\{\therefore\right.$ In $\mathrm{I}^{\text {st }}$ quadrant $\tan$ is positive $\}$
(II) Now, $\cot 22.5^{\circ}=\frac{1}{\tan 22.5^{\circ}}=\frac{1}{-1+\sqrt{2}}=1+\sqrt{2}$ which is also an irrational number.

questions.q:
If $p \tan \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)=q \tan \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right)$, then what is $\frac{(p+q)}{(p-q)}$
equal to? equal to?
questions.solution:
We have.
$\begin{aligned}
& p \tan \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)=q \tan \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{p}{q}=\frac{\tan \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right)}{\tan \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)} \\
& =\frac{\sin \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \cos \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)}{\cos \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \sin \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)}
\end{aligned}$
Using componendo and dividendo rule,
$\begin{gathered}
\Rightarrow \frac{p+q}{p-q}=\frac{\sin \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \cos \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)+\cos \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \sin \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)}{\sin \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \cos \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)-\cos \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \sin \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{p+q}{p-q}=\frac{\sin \left[\left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right)+\left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)\right]}{\sin \left[\left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right)-\left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)\right]}=\frac{\sin \left(90^{\circ}+2 \theta\right)}{\sin \left(150^{\circ}\right)} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{p+q}{p-q}=\frac{\sin \left(90^{\circ}+2 \theta\right)}{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}=2 \cos 2 \theta
\end{gathered}$

questions.q: Let $\theta$ be the angle between two unit vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. If $\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $5 \vec{a}-4 \vec{b}$, then what is $\cos \theta+\cos 2 \theta$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Since, $(\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}) \&(5 \vec{a}-4 \vec{b})$ are perpendicular vectors.
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow(\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}) \cdot(5 \vec{a}-4 \vec{b})=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 5|\vec{a}|^2-4 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+10 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-8|\vec{b}|^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 5 \times 1+6 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-8=0 \quad \text { Since, }|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=1 \\
& \Rightarrow 6|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \cos \theta=3 \\
& \Rightarrow 1 \cdot 1 \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}$
So, $\cos 2 \theta=2 \cos ^2 \theta-1=2 \times \frac{1}{4}-1=-\frac{1}{2}$
Now, $\cos \theta+\cos 2 \theta=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=0$

questions.q: What is $3 \alpha+2 \beta$ equal to if $(2 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+27 \hat{k}) \times(\hat{i}+\alpha \hat{j}+\beta \hat{k})$ is a null vector?
questions.solution:
Given that, $(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+27 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \times(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\alpha \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\beta \hat{\mathrm{k}})=0\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\
2 & 6 & 27 \\
1 & \alpha & \beta
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \hat{i}(6 \beta-27 \alpha)-\hat{j}(2 \beta-27)+\hat{k}(2 \alpha-6)=0
\end{aligned}$
Comparing both sides of above equation, we get:-
$\begin{aligned}
& 6 \beta-27 \alpha=0 \Rightarrow 2 \beta=9 \alpha \\
& 2 \beta-27=0 \Rightarrow \beta=\frac{27}{2} \text { and } 2 \alpha-6=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=3
\end{aligned}$
So, $3 \alpha+2 \beta=3 \times 3+2 \times \frac{27}{2}=9+27=36$
